title: nsight-cuda-graph-timeline-investigation-feb-2025
content:
Purpose:
This is a running investigation into unexpected low SM utilization and fluctuating occupancy on our production transformer inference image when running with CUDA Graphs enabled. Quick summary: with CUDA Graph capture turned on we see lower sustained SM utilization (avg ~46%) vs capture disabled (~72%) for the same batch/seq config. We need to document observations, hypotheses, quick experiments, and next steps so eng and SRE can triage impact on latency SLOs.

Test config (replicable):
- Model: rwd-base-3B (FP16, qlinear-fused path)
- Inference mode: streaming token-by-token generation
- Hardware: A100-SXM4-40GB, driver 535.86, CUDA 12.2
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.24.0 (branch: cuda-graph-experiments)
- Invocation pattern: batch size 8, seq_len=2048, decode steps=128
- Capture window: warmup 4 tokens, then capture on token 5 for the next 64 tokens
- Nsight sessions: full range kernel timeline + API trace captured

Observed artifacts from Nsight (session sg-1792):
- Timeline shows frequent idle gaps between large GEMM kernels when capture is enabled. These gaps are ~120-180 microseconds each and coincide with host-side memcpy / stream synchronization events in the API trace.
- Kernel durations: cutlass_gemm_kernel (mix of small and large GEMMs) shows variable runtime; some launches finish in 400us, others in 1.1ms depending on input shape after kv-cache update.
- SM occupancy (sampled per-kernel): median occupancy for cutlass kernels ~0.42 (42%), theoretical occupancy expected ~0.72 for same launch config based on register/shared memory usage estimates from nvcc --ptxas-options.
- Warp execution stalls: memory dependency stalls high (~40% of cycles stalled) on softmax and layernorm kernels.
- cudaMemcpyAsync host->device periods are visible inside capture windows and appear to serialize execution when pinned memory fallback occurs (look for H2D copies flagged as pageable in the API trace).

Key hypotheses (ranked):
1) Capture-induced stream ordering side-effects: when we capture in CUDA Graphs, some host-driven small H2D transfers (KV updates, prompt prep) end up serialized on the stream that the graph replays on, causing gaps between kernels. Evidence: API trace shows memcpy events with flags that match fallback to pageable copy; these align with the idle gaps.
2) Kernel launch configuration degeneracy under capture: the graph engine may change how kernels are scheduled across SMs (less interleaving) leading to lower occupancy. Evidence: kernels show less overlapping of compute and memcpy compared to the uncaptured run.
3) Sub-optimal memory access pattern increasing memory dependency stalls in softmax/layernorm when replayed from the graph; maybe data alignment differs when pinned allocation pool differs under graph capture.
4) cuBLAS/cuDNN internal fallback behavior when called within a graph replay path (less likely but recorded in some traces as different code paths).

Short experiments we ran (and results):
- Toggle CUDA Graph capture on/off with identical warmup and identical streams (captured in sg-1784). Result: capture OFF -> steady SM utilization ~72%, capture ON -> drops to ~46%. Latency p50 increased by ~18% with capture ON.
- Force all H2D copies to use cudaHostAlloc/pinned memory instead of malloc+cudaMemcpyAsync (patch in PR #2781). Result: gaps reduced by ~65%, SM utilization rose to ~60% (better but still below uncaptured baseline).
- Change capture window to exclude the token where KV write happens (capture tokens 10..74 instead of 5..69). Result: improvements similar to pinned memory change — suggests KV updates falling into capture window are a major factor.
- Flip streams for async H2D to stream 2 while capture uses stream 0, but graph capture rebinds to stream 0 at replay (confirmed in API trace). No effect.

Detailed timeline note (example slice):
- T=0: kernel A (cutlass_fwd) runs (450us)
- T=450us: short gap (140us) where API trace shows cudaMemcpyAsync host->device of ~48KB using pageable memory
- T=590us: kernel B (softmax) runs (260us) but shows high mem dependency stalls
- T=850us: kernel C (kv_write) runs (30us)
- T=880us: idle gap 160us (graph replay appears to wait for host semaphore)
- T=1040us: next batch of GEMMs start
Observations: the gaps are enough to reduce inter-kernel overlap and reduce effective occupancy.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does capture change host->device behavior (pinned vs fallback)? Is it our allocator, or an interaction with the runtime when capture is active?
- Are there cuBLAS/cuDNN internal heuristics that detect replay mode and alter workspace allocation? Need to check vendor docs and warp-level traces.
- Could the graph replay be implicitly inserting streamWaitEvent on host or using a different synchronization primitive? API trace shows deviceSynchronize-like waits but not clearly attributed.

Immediate recommendations (quick wins):
1) Make H2D host buffers pinned by default for all token-level KV updates in the serving runtime experiment branch (we already validated uplift). This reduces serialization and is low risk (PR #2781).
2) Adjust capture windows to avoid the single-token KV updates — capture only steady-state decode tokens where no host interaction occurs. Not a long-term solution but buys time for deeper fixes.
3) Add an allocator-mode toggle and runtime flag to force pinned allocations for capture-enabled deployments; expose as config in the edge-case feature flag console to target canary users.

Longer-term investigations and actions:
- Instrument allocator and add a small tracer to record whether an H2D copy used pinned vs pageable memory at runtime (tie to logs and nsight markers). Create ticket JIRA-RINF-1894 to track.
- Run a controlled microbenchmark: isolate a minimal capture graph that does KV write + GEMM sequences to test if behavior is reproducible without the full model. If reproducible, we can open a vendor support SR with a deterministic repro.
- Profile with per-SM telemetry (nsight's per-SM counters) to see if specific SMs are starved or if there's a scheduling imbalance.
- Evaluate kernel fusion opportunities (merge small kernels) to reduce kernel-launch overheads inside captures — especially the numerous small memory-bound kernels that contribute to stalls.
- Run experiments on a different GPU family (H100) to see if scheduling heuristics differ under capture.

Action items (owners):
- Sofia: land pinned allocation flag (PR #2781) behind feature flag + smoke tests. (ETA 2d)
- Daniel: write microbenchmark capture repro and collect raw repro artifacts for vendor SR (ETA 3d).
- Priya: add nsight-perf-counters run for SM-level telemetry and share results (ETA 5d).
- Ethan: instrument allocator logs and add small tracing markers around H2D ops (ETA 4d).

Notes to self / rough checklist:
- Capture sessions to attach: sg-1792 (main), sg-1784 (toggle test), sg-1803 (pinned mem test)
- Keep PR #2781 small: just allocator + feature flag + test script
- Verify that pinned memory pool size is bounded (don't OOM host) — add metrics to console.
- Talk to vendor rep about whether cudaGraph replay can change stream semantics or implicitly serialize host-driven memcpy on replay stream.

Conclusion:
There is convincing evidence that host-side H2D copies and capture interaction are the dominant cause of the observed occupancy drop. Pinned-memory and moving KV-write out of the capture window both materially improve utilization. Next steps are to harden the fix, produce a minimal repro for vendor support, and run per-SM telemetry to rule out deeper kernel scheduling pathologies.

Appendix (commands & quick notes):
- Nsight CLI to capture (example): nsight-cu-cli --capture-mode timeline --target-process <pid> --output ./sg-1792.nsc 
- Quick check for pageable copy in API trace: look for cudaMemcpyAsync entries without "cudaHostAlloc" or for calls that map to host pointer mnemonics from malloc().
- Relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2781 (allocator change, feature flag "enable_pinned_for_graphs")
- Jira: JIRA-RINF-1894 (track capture/allocator investigation)

If you want, I can extract the small repro branch and push a docker image with capture-on and pinned-off/pinned-on toggles for SRE to run load tests against canary cluster.
